project_id.description: Bedrock project ID scoping the Mantle sub-surface (OpenAI-compatible gpt-*/Gemma routing) via the OpenAI-Project header. When empty, AWS routes to the account's default project. No effect on the Converse/bedrock-runtime paths (can use env. prefix)

endpoints.description: Interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) hosts to dial instead of the public regional endpoints. Use the endpoint's DNS name from the VPC console, not the endpoint ID — AWS appends a random string that cannot be derived. Region is still required: it sets the SigV4 credential scope.

mantle.description: Host for the bedrock-mantle service (can use env. prefix)

sagemaker_key_config.description: AWS credentials and routing for SageMaker real-time endpoints. Leave access_key and secret_key empty to use the default AWS credential chain.

access_key.description: AWS access key used to mint bearer tokens (can use env. prefix)

secret_key.description: AWS secret key (can use env. prefix)

session_token.description: AWS session token for temporary credentials (can use env. prefix)

region.description: AWS region of the endpoints; a model id may override it with a region prefix

role_arn.description: AWS IAM role ARN for AssumeRole (can use env. prefix)

external_id.description: External ID for AssumeRole (can use env. prefix)

session_name.description: Role session name for AssumeRole (can use env. prefix)

endpoints.description: Runtime host override, e.g. an interface VPC endpoint, FIPS or dual-stack host. Region is still required.

runtime.description: Host for the SageMaker runtime (can use env. prefix)

url.description: VLLM server base URL (can use env. prefix)

model_name.description: Exact model name served on this VLLM instance

databricks_key_config.description: Databricks key configuration. Required on every key of a databricks provider.

workspace_url.description: Databricks workspace URL, e.g. https://dbc-1234abcd-5678.cloud.databricks.com (can use env. prefix). A scheme and trailing path are tolerated.

api_format.description: Which Databricks inference surface to target. 'model_serving' uses /serving-endpoints; 'ai_gateway' uses /ai-gateway/mlflow/v1; 'auto' (default) picks by model name — a dotted name such as system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5 goes to the AI Gateway, anything else to Model Serving.

client_id.description: OAuth M2M service principal client ID (can use env. prefix). Set together with client_secret, and leave the key value empty, to authenticate without a personal access token.

client_secret.description: OAuth M2M service principal client secret (can use env. prefix)

forward_gateway_tags.description: Forward Bifrost governance labels (virtual key, team, customer names) to Databricks as the Databricks-Ai-Gateway-Request-Tags header for usage attribution.

scopes.description: OAuth M2M scopes requested when minting a token (default: ["all-apis"]). Set this when the service principal's OAuth secret was created with scopes. Databricks rejects a token request that names any scope the secret does not have. Model Serving needs model-serving, Unity AI Gateway needs ai-gateway, and /v1/decisions needs ai-functions.

cloudflare_key_config.description: Cloudflare key configuration. Required on every key of a cloudflare provider.

account_id.description: Cloudflare account ID that serves Workers AI (can use env. prefix)

oauth_key_config.description: OAuth-minted bearer for OpenAI-compatible providers, including custom providers built on the openai base. Set this and leave value empty: Bifrost mints the access token from the token endpoint, caches it per credential and refreshes it before expiry. A non-empty value always wins.

grant_type.description: client_credentials (RFC 6749 §4.4) or jwt_bearer (RFC 7523: Bifrost signs an assertion with private_key).

token_url.description: Token endpoint, absolute https URL (plain http is accepted for loopback hosts only; can use env. prefix). Must not carry userinfo, a query or a fragment; send extra parameters through extra_params.

client_id.description: client_credentials: client ID (can use env. prefix)

client_secret.description: client_credentials: client secret (can use env. prefix)

private_key.description: jwt_bearer: RSA or EC private key in PEM form (can use env. prefix)

audience.description: jwt_bearer: aud claim (required); client_credentials: optional audience form parameter

key_id.description: jwt_bearer: kid header, when the server selects keys by id

auth_style.description: client_credentials: send the client credentials as HTTP Basic auth (header) or as form fields (body)

extra_params.description: Extra form parameters sent on the token request

assertion_lifetime_seconds.description: jwt_bearer: seconds from issue until the assertion expires (exp = now + value); 0 or omitted uses the default of 300. iat is backdated by 30 seconds for clock skew, so the assertion's exp - iat span is this value plus 30.

anthropic_key_config.description: Anthropic key configuration, for anthropic and custom providers built on the anthropic base.

workload_identity.description: Workload Identity Federation. Set this and leave value empty: Bifrost exchanges an OIDC identity token for a short-lived Anthropic access token. A non-empty value always wins.

federation_rule_id.description: Federation rule ID, fdrl_... (can use env. prefix)

organization_id.description: Anthropic organization UUID (can use env. prefix)

service_account_id.description: Service account the minted token acts as, svac_... (can use env. prefix)

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, wrkspc_...; required when the rule spans several workspaces (can use env. prefix)

oneOf.description: Legacy shape: a bare provider-specific identifier. Equivalent to {"model_id": "<value>"}.

model_id.description: Provider-specific identifier sent on the wire (deployment name, inference profile ID, fine-tuned model ID, etc.).

model_name.description: Canonical model name used for pricing, logging, and family inference.

model_family.description: Underlying model family. Used by provider routing without substring-sniffing the wire model ID.

region.description: Per-alias region override (can use env. prefix).

api_version.description: Azure OpenAI api-version override for this alias.

anthropic_version.description: Azure anthropic-version header override for Claude-on-Azure deployments.

endpoint.description: Per-alias Azure endpoint override (can use env. prefix).

use_speech_endpoints.description: Per-alias Azure override of use_speech_endpoints: send this alias's speech and transcription requests to Azure AI Speech instead of Azure OpenAI.

use_voice_live_endpoints.description: Per-alias Azure override of use_voice_live_endpoints: send this alias's realtime WebSocket sessions to Azure Voice Live instead of Azure OpenAI.

project_id.description: Per-alias project override shared across providers: Vertex uses it as the GCP project; Bedrock and Bedrock Mantle send it as the AWS project via the OpenAI-Project / anthropic-workspace-id header (can use env. prefix).

project_number.description: Per-alias Vertex project number override (can use env. prefix).

inference_profile_arn.description: Per-alias Bedrock inference profile ARN (can use env. prefix).

use_deployments_endpoint.description: Replicate: use the deployments endpoint instead of the predictions endpoint for this alias.

deployment_url.description: Baseten: OpenAI-compatible base URL of a dedicated deployment. Requests for this alias go there instead of Model APIs, and model_id is the served model name (Engine-Builder and BEI deployments ignore it). Must be https (can use env. prefix).

use_anthropic_endpoints.description: Routes chat completions and responses requests through Anthropic-compatible endpoints.

aliases.description: Model alias mappings: each entry maps a user-facing model name to either a bare provider identifier (legacy string shape) or an AliasConfig object carrying the wire identifier plus optional canonical name, family, and provider-specific overrides.

base_url.description: Base URL for the provider (optional, required for Ollama)

extra_headers.description: Additional headers to send with requests

default_request_timeout_in_seconds.description: Default request timeout in seconds. For streaming requests this bounds the connection, the request write and the wait for response headers; once headers arrive, stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds governs the body.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable TLS certificate verification for provider connections. This bypasses server certificate validation and should be used only as a last resort when a trusted CA chain cannot be configured. Prefer ca_cert_pem for self-signed or private CA deployments.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for provider endpoint connections (e.g. self-signed or internal CA). Supports inline PEM or env.VAR_NAME.

stream_idle_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle timeout per stream chunk in seconds. If no data is received for this many seconds, the stream is closed. Default: 60.

keep_alive_timeout_in_seconds.description: Idle keep-alive for pooled connections, in seconds. Set below the upstream server's keep-alive so Bifrost drops idle connections before the server closes them. Default: 30.

max_conns_per_host.description: Maximum number of TCP connections per provider host. For HTTP/2 (e.g. Bedrock), each connection supports ~100 concurrent streams. Default: 5000.

enforce_http2.description: Force HTTP/2 on provider connections (relevant for Bedrock and other net/http-based providers)

http2_ping_interval_in_seconds.description: Seconds of stream idle before a client-initiated HTTP/2 keepalive PING (0 = disabled; only when enforce_http2).

beta_header_overrides.description: Override default Anthropic beta header support per provider. Keys are header prefixes (e.g. 'redact-thinking-'), values are true (supported) or false (unsupported). Headers not listed use the built-in defaults.

allow_private_network.description: Allow connections to RFC 1918 private IPs (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x). Enable for providers on a k8s pod network, LAN, or private VPC. Loopback addresses (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) remain allowed regardless of this setting. Link-local addresses (169.254.x.x) are always blocked.

url.description: URL of the proxy server (supports env.VAR_NAME or a literal URI)

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for TLS connections through the proxy (for SSL-intercepting proxies, supports env.VAR_NAME)

virtualKeyProviderConfig.description: Provider configuration for a virtual key

allowed_models.description: Allowed models for this provider config. Use ["*"] to allow all models; empty array denies all (deny-by-default). An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

blacklisted_models.description: Models blocked for this provider config even if matched by allowed_models. Use ["*"] to block all; empty array blocks none. An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

key_ids.description: Key identifiers allowed for this provider config. Use ["*"] to allow all keys; empty array denies all (deny-by-default).

keys.description: Provider keys for this config (empty means all keys allowed for this provider)

value.description: API key value (can use env. prefix)

models.description: Models this key can access. Use ["*"] to allow all models; empty array denies all (deny-by-default). An entry starting with regex: is an RE2 pattern matched case-insensitively against the whole model name.

client_id.description: Azure client ID for authentication (can use env. prefix)

client_secret.description: Azure client secret for authentication (can use env. prefix)

tenant_id.description: Azure tenant ID for authentication (can use env. prefix)

use_speech_endpoints.description: Send speech and transcription requests to Azure AI Speech (SSML text to speech, fast transcription) instead of Azure OpenAI.

use_voice_live_endpoints.description: Send realtime WebSocket sessions to Azure Voice Live (/voice-live/realtime) instead of Azure OpenAI. The WebRTC and client secret routes reject it.

project_id.description: Google Cloud project ID (can use env. prefix)

force_single_region.description: When true, always call the configured region and skip automatic promotion of multi-region-only models to a multi-region endpoint. Enable for provisioned throughput.

use_session_routing.description: Send each request's prompt_cache_key to Gemini models as session_id. Vertex routes requests with the same session ID to one replica, so they reuse its implicit cache. Enable only if Google has turned on session routing for this key's project.

aws_workload_identity.description: GCP Workload Identity Federation from the workload's AWS identity (EKS IRSA / Pod Identity, ECS task role, EC2 instance profile, AWS_* env vars). Takes precedence over auth_credentials; the two must not be combined.

audience.description: Workload Identity Pool provider resource name, e.g. //iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL_ID/providers/PROVIDER_ID (can use env. prefix)

service_account_email.description: Service account to impersonate after federation. Omit to use the federated principal directly (can use env. prefix)

token_lifetime_seconds.description: Lifetime of the impersonated service-account token in seconds. Only used with service_account_email. Default 3600. Lifetimes above 3600 require the target service account to be allowed by the organization policy constraint constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension; otherwise token generation fails.

aws_region.description: AWS region used to sign the STS GetCallerIdentity request. Defaults to AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, then instance metadata (can use env. prefix)

aws_role_arn.description: Optional IAM role to assume with the workload's credentials before the GCP exchange (can use env. prefix)

access_key.description: AWS access key (can use env. prefix)

secret_key.description: AWS secret key (can use env. prefix)

session_token.description: AWS session token (can use env. prefix)

role_arn.description: AWS IAM role ARN for AssumeRole (can use env. prefix)

external_id.description: External ID for AssumeRole (can use env. prefix)

session_name.description: Role session name for AssumeRole (can use env. prefix)

batch_role_arn.description: Service role ARN passed to Bedrock batch jobs for S3 access; takes priority over any role_arn sent in the request (can use env. prefix)

batch_s3_config.description: S3 bucket configuration for Bedrock batch operations

prefix.description: S3 key prefix for batch files

is_default.description: Whether this is the default bucket for batch operations

endpoints.description: Interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) hosts to dial instead of the public regional endpoints. Use the endpoint's DNS name from the VPC console, not the endpoint ID — AWS appends a random string that cannot be derived. Region is still required: it sets the SigV4 credential scope.

runtime.description: Host for the bedrock-runtime service, which serves all inference (can use env. prefix)

control_plane.description: Host for the bedrock service, which serves model listing and batch jobs (can use env. prefix)

mantle.description: Host for the bedrock-mantle service, which serves mantle-routed models (can use env. prefix)

agent_runtime.description: Host for the bedrock-agent-runtime service, which serves rerank (can use env. prefix)

s3.description: Host for the s3 service, which serves batch file I/O. Must carry the literal "bucket." prefix, since Bifrost prepends the bucket name to build the virtual-hosted URL. A Gateway endpoint needs no value here (can use env. prefix)

url.description: VLLM server base URL (can use env. prefix)

model_name.description: Exact model name served on this VLLM instance

scim_attribute_role_mappings.description: List of attribute -> role mappings. When a user resolves to more than one role (from these mappings, the native roles claim, or group/attribute channels), roleResolutionStrategy decides which single role is assigned: 'highestPermissionCount' (default) picks the role with the most permissions; 'order' evaluates this mappings list top to bottom and the first matching rule wins.

attribute.description: JWT claim name (supports dot paths, e.g. 'realm_access.roles')

role.description: Bifrost role to assign on match

scim_role_resolution_strategy.description: How a single role is chosen when a user resolves to more than one role: 'highestPermissionCount' (default) picks the role with the most permissions; 'order' evaluates the attribute-role mappings top to bottom and the first matching rule wins.

scim_access_profile_resolution_strategy.description: How many attribute-access-profile grants a user receives when several attributeAccessProfileMappings match: 'all' (default) grants every matching rule's profile; 'order' grants only the profiles of the first rule, in list order, that the user matches. Profiles granted through roles are unaffected.

scim_workload_identity.description: Workload identity on this SSO provider: token issuers, besides the provider itself, whose workload tokens can be mapped to service accounts.

scim_trusted_issuer.description: A token issuer whose workload tokens, addressed to one of its audiences, can authenticate the service accounts they are mapped to. Workloads are mapped to service accounts in the dashboard or through the API, not in this file.

name.description: Name of the issuer, unique among the provider's issuers ignoring case, e.g. 'AWS prod'. Mappings refer to the issuer by this name: renaming or removing it leaves them without an issuer until one with the name is back.

kind.description: 'aws' trusts AWS STS outbound identity federation tokens, named by IAM role ARN. 'generic' trusts any OIDC issuer and takes identityClaim and machineCheck from this entry; with machineCheck 'any' it takes only tokens whose identity claim is mapped; a rule is required to map the SSO app's own client ID, which people's tokens also carry.

issuerUrl.description: The issuer exactly as tokens carry it in iss: https, or http only on localhost for local testing, with no user info, query or fragment. Signing keys are found through its OIDC discovery document. A mapping made on this issuer stops working if the URL changes.

audiences.description: Audiences a workload token must be addressed to, typically this Bifrost's URL.

identityClaim.description: For 'generic', required: the claim whose value names the workload, e.g. client_id or sub. Values are matched exactly. A mapping made on this issuer stops working if the claim changes.

machineCheck.description: For 'generic', required: how a workload's token is told from a person's. 'any' when the issuer only issues to workloads, or when only mapped workload IDs should be taken; otherwise a rule only workload tokens pass, e.g. Okta sub_equals_claim cid, Auth0 claim_equals gty client-credentials, Keycloak claim_prefix preferred_username service-account-.

claim.description: The claim the rule reads. Required for every kind but 'any'.

value.description: The value, or prefix, the claim must have. Required for claim_equals and claim_prefix; an empty one would match every token.

maxLifetimeSeconds.description: Longest total token lifetime accepted. Defaults to 24 hours.

disabled.description: Set to true to keep the issuer and its mappings but refuse its tokens.

scim_claims_sync_mode.description: When SCIM is enabled, selects whether IdP login/refresh claims still drive role/team/business-unit/profile sync and JIT user creation: 'both' (default) keeps syncing from both claims and SCIM; 'scim' makes SCIM the sole source of truth — claims are ignored for provisioning and new users must be pushed by SCIM. Inert when SCIM is disabled (claims always sync then).

scim_attribute_team_mappings.description: Attribute -> team mappings (all matches apply). Use value '*' for pass-through.

value.description: Claim value to match, or '*' for pass-through

team.description: Bifrost team slug to assign. In case of '*' value, leave this empty

project.description: A project declared under governance.projects: what it allows, what it may spend, and how that is divided between its members. Members themselves are added from the dashboard or the API.

name.description: Unique project name. Requests reference it with the x-bf-project-name header; the reconciler matches the declaration to the stored project by this name.

is_active.description: Whether the project allows and accounts for anything

expires_at.description: When the project stops allowing anything; omit to never expire

access_rule.description: How the project's own access composes with the access a caller already holds: union leaves the caller's own access untouched (a project with no provider config then only accounts for spend), intersect permits only what both allow.

membership_mode.description: explicit consults the membership rows; open lets any caller opt in. An open project cannot divide its budget between members.

accounting_mode.description: Which ledgers a request's spend lands on: the project's, the calling principal's, or both

split_policy.description: How the budgets and rate limits the project holds, at every tier (its own, each provider's, and each model's), are divided between members: none leaves them shared, equal gives every member an equal share of each. A change to an equal split's roster or caps recomputes every share in the background.

calendar_aligned.description: Snap the project's budget and rate-limit reset windows to calendar boundaries (day, week, month, quarter, year) instead of rolling from first use. Windows shorter than a day cannot be aligned and stay rolling.

allow_all_providers.description: Grant access to every provider, including ones without a provider_configs entry and providers added later. Listed providers keep their own model, key, budget, and rate-limit rules.

disable_content_logging.description: Per-project override of content logging for requests scoped to this project. Omit to inherit what the request's virtual key decides, or client.disableContentLogging when the key has no setting. The project's value overrides the virtual key's in both directions.

budgets.description: Project-level spend caps. Declared without ids: on a change, a budget is matched to its stored row by reset_duration so its accumulated spend and window carry over.

provider_configs.description: Per-provider access and accounting, one entry per provider

project_budget.description: A spend cap on a project, a provider inside it, or a model under that provider

reset_duration.description: Reset window, e.g. "1M", "1h", "1Q". Also what pairs a declared budget with its stored row on a change.

reset_config.description: Window settings the reset duration cannot express. Only valid when reset_duration is quarterly ("1Q").

quarter_start_month.description: First month of Q1 as 1-12. Omitted or 0 means January.

project_rate_limit.description: A request and token rate limit on a project, a provider inside it, or a model under that provider. A cap is enforced only with its window, and a limit with neither pair enforces nothing, so at least one complete pair is required.

token_max_limit.description: Maximum number of tokens allowed in the reset window

request_max_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed in the reset window

provider_name.description: Provider name. A project names each provider at most once; on a change the entry is matched to its stored row by this name.

all_models_allowed.description: Whether all models under this provider are allowed

allowed_models.description: Allowed model names (ignored when all_models_allowed is true)

blacklisted_models.description: Models blocked for this provider even if matched by allowed_models (denylist wins). Use ["*"] to block all; empty array or omitted blocks none.

key_ids.description: Key IDs allowed for this provider. Use ["*"] to allow all keys; empty array or omitted allows none, regardless of the top-level version. Specific IDs restrict access to those keys only, and each must belong to this provider.

weight.description: Load-balancer seed weight for this provider (null opts out of weighted routing / no override)

budgets.description: Spend caps on this provider inside the project

model_budgets.description: Per-model budgets and rate limits under this provider, at most one entry per model

project_provider_model_budget.description: Per-model budget group under a project provider config, with optional per-model rate limit

model_name.description: Model this budget group applies to (scoped to the parent provider). The "*" tier is not accepted here; the provider's own budgets cover it.

scim_attribute_access_profile_mappings.description: Attribute -> access-profile mappings. Every matching rule applies: the user is granted the union of the profiles it matches, on top of any profile assigned by role or from the dashboard. Bifrost keeps the tightest limit across the granted profiles.

attribute.description: JWT claim name (supports dot paths, e.g. 'realm_access.roles')

value.description: Claim value to match (case-insensitive). '*' matches whenever the claim carries any non-empty value; glob patterns (e.g. 'bifrost-*') are also supported.

accessProfile.description: Name of the access profile (defined in bifrost.accessProfiles) to grant on match

scim_attribute_project_mappings.description: Attribute -> project mappings. Every matching rule applies: the user is added to each project it matches. Projects are never auto-created; a rule naming a missing project is dropped. Memberships added this way are removed when the rule stops matching; members added from the dashboard are kept.

attribute.description: JWT claim name (supports dot paths, e.g. 'realm_access.roles')

value.description: Claim value to match (case-insensitive). '*' matches whenever the claim carries any non-empty value; glob patterns (e.g. 'bifrost-*') are also supported.

project.description: Name of the project to add the user to on match

scim_bulk_sync_interval.description: How often the directory reconcile lists the IdP's users through its admin API and deprovisions the ones it no longer returns, as whole days or h/m/s pairs (e.g. '12h', '1h30m', '7d'). Must be between 1h and 30d. Defaults to 24h. Inert when SCIM provisioning is enabled or the provider has no directory API access (e.g. Okta without apiToken).

value.description: Claim value to match. Wildcard '*' will use the claim as the name of the business unit to assign.

business_unit.description: Bifrost business unit slug to assign. In case of '*' value, leave this empty

scim_claim_attributes.description: Per-claim SCIM interpretation. Maps each claim name to its SCIM source type and attribute key. Set by the UI when SCIM provisioning is configured.

attributeType.description: 'user' reads from SCIM User resource attributes; 'group' matches SCIM Group resource.

attributeValue.description: SCIM attribute key or group match field for this claim.

scim_provisioning_token.description: Bearer token that inbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning clients (the IdP's SCIM app) must present in the Authorization header to push users and groups to Bifrost. Normally minted in the dashboard (Governance -> User Provisioning) and shown once, but may be seeded here for declarative/GitOps deployments; supports the env. prefix for environment-variable references. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='

scim_auth_proxy.description: Identity-aware proxy (IAP) fronting this SCIM/SSO provider — e.g. Cloudflare Access, a generic OIDC proxy, or AWS ALB (Zero Trust / ZTNA). When enabled, Bifrost takes the login credential from the proxy's header and validates it against the proxy's own keys (not the IdP's), then feeds the resulting claims into the active provider's mapping. Shared across every provider. Renders into scim_config.config.authProxy.

enabled.description: Turn the auth-proxy layer on. When false the rest of this block is ignored.

provider.description: Proxy type. 'cloudflare-access' and 'generic' validate OIDC RS256 tokens via JWKS; 'aws-alb' validates ES256 tokens from an AWS ALB via the regional per-kid public key.

mode.description: 'login_only' (default) authenticates an already-provisioned user by identity (email/sub) without deriving permissions from the token. 'full' also runs attribute→role/team/business-unit mapping from the proxy token's claims — the IdP claims used for mapping must be passed through into the proxy-signed token.

headerName.description: Request header carrying the proxy token. Defaults per provider (cloudflare-access: Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion, aws-alb: x-amzn-oidc-data); required for the generic provider. Supports the env. prefix.

issuerUrl.description: Proxy issuer URL, e.g. https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com. Required for the cloudflare-access and generic providers; must be https. Supports the env. prefix.

jwksUrl.description: Explicit JWKS URL for JWKS providers. Derived from issuerUrl for cloudflare-access; empty means OIDC discovery from the issuer (generic). Must be https. Supports the env. prefix.

audience.description: Expected token audience (aud) for JWKS providers, binding the token to this application. Required unless allowedAudiences is set. Supports the env. prefix.

allowedAudiences.description: Alternative to a single audience: a list of accepted audiences. Must not contain blank entries.

region.description: AWS ALB only: region for the public-key endpoint. Derived from the signer ARN when empty. Supports the env. prefix.

expectedSigner.description: AWS ALB only: the ALB ARN to pin the token's signer to. Required for the aws-alb provider — the regional key signs tokens for every ALB in the region, so without this pin any ALB could mint an accepted token. Supports the env. prefix.

publicKeyBaseUrl.description: AWS ALB only: override base URL for the public-key endpoint (keys fetched from <base>/<kid>). Needed for partitions like GovCloud whose endpoint differs from the standard region-derived URL; must be https. Supports the env. prefix.

userIdClaim.description: Token claim used as the user identity. Default 'email'. Supports the env. prefix.
